text.p: The Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) agreed on Thursday to freeze output at 25.03 million barrels per day.
Following is the full text of the communique issued at the end of the meeting in Vienna as carried by the OPECNA news agency, monitored in London:
The 101st meeting of the conference of the Organisation of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) was held in Vienna, Austria, from 27th to 28th November, 1996.

The conference unanimously elected HE Abdalla Salem el-Badri, Secretary of the General People's Committee of Energy of the Socialist People's Libyan Arab Jamahiriya and head of its delegation, as its president. HE Abdullah Bin Hamad Al Attiyah, Minister Of Energy and Industry Of Qatar and Head Of its Delegation, was unanimously elected alternate president.

The conference appointed Mr. Saddam Zabin Hassan, governor for Iraq, as chairman of the board of governors for the year 1997, and Miss Siham Razouki, governor for Kuwait, to be alternate chairman for the same period.
The conference reviewed the secretary general's report, the report of the economic commission board, the report of the ministerial monitoring sub-committee and various administrative matters.

The conference decided to reconstitute the ministerial monitoring sub-committee under the continued chairmanship of HE Gholamreza Aghazadeh, Minister of Petroleum of the I.R. Iran, with HE Ida Bagus Sudjana, minister of mines and energy of Indonesia, HE Chief Dan Etete, minister of petroleum resources of Nigeria, and He Dr. Rilwanu Lukman, secretary general, as members.

The conference, having reviewed the market situation, agreed to roll over until the end of June, 1997 the current overall supply ceiling of 25.033 mb/d and individual member countries allocations, to which all member countries reiterated their commitment.
The conference approved the budget of the organisation for the year 1997.

The conference expressed its deepest appreciation and gratitude for the services rendered to the organisation by Dr. Ramzi Salman, the outgoing deputy secretary general, whose term of office will come to an end on 3rd March, 1997, and thanked him for the active and positive contribution which he had made to its work.

The conference expressed its appreciation to the government of the Federal Republic of Austria and to the authorities of the city of Vienna for their warm hospitality and the excellent arrangements made for the meeting, and extended its warm thanks to HE Dr. Martin Bartenstein, minister for environment, youth and family affairs, for the gracious invitation extended to them.
The conference passed resolutions which will be published on 28th December, 1996, after ratification by member countries.
The next ordinary meeting of the conference will be convened in Vienna on 25th June, 1997.
